title: SRLV Coverage Audit
standfirst: SRLV holds maedi-visna virus of sheep and caprine arthritis-encephalitis virus of goats, which are one continuum rather than two clean species. Five features, all with profiles — including tat, which in this genus is not what its name suggests.

sections.title: What the module calls
sections.lede: Five features, and a tat that is collinear rather than spliced.

blocks.html: SRLV tat is a single-exon protein, also published as S, and it was MEASURED collinear by tblastn of each deposited protein against its own genome rather than assumed spliced from the HIV-1 layout. It therefore gets a PSSM and a copy_num like any other feature. EIAV tat, in the sister module, is genuinely spliced and gets neither.

sections.title: Where it does not call, and why

blocks.html: No declared feature lacks a profile. rev appears in the vocabulary and bins to its own key, but the module does not declare it: it is spliced, and nothing here calls spliced features.

85.5% of the 475 deposited features from this module's taxa are bound by a naming rule. The remainder are recorded in UNASSIGNED and DISCARDED: the first is vocabulary no rule reached, the second is records the source itself calls partial or truncated, which the project discards rather than trains on.

Coverage is measured by annotating de-replicated exemplars through the real GTO pipeline — annotate_by_viral_pssm-GTO.pl, then the transcript-edit and splice passes, then viral_genome_quality.pl — not by a reimplementation. Spliced features are included, which the flat feature-table path cannot represent. Rates are per exemplar, and exemplars are clustered at 95% nucleotide identity, so one row is one distinct sequence rather than one deposit.

source_note: Measured 27 October 2026 from the shipped module: the SRLV block of Viral_PSSM.json, its profiles and collections, and the 27 October coverage re-annotation over 51 exemplars de-replicated from 265 genomes. Vocabulary figures come from collections/synonyms.tsv, written by the module's own builder from the naming rules, and count deposited features rather than unique sequences.
